decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch the right wrist toward a top-down mouse approach, using small continuous elbow-up movements.
Advance above the mouse while completing downward wrist pitch; preserve open fingers and clearance.
Lower the right fingers around the mouse, completing the vertical approach; grasp alignment remains visual.
Center the mouse between the right fingers and close; retention will be checked during a small lift.
Lift with the mouse held closed and translate rightward toward the mouse pad, checking visual retention.
The mouse remained on the table. Reopen and return with a lower, slightly forward grasp alignment.
Clear the mouse before recentering leftward; approach vertically to avoid pushing it sideways.
Lower slightly with the mouse centered between open fingers, then close and pause for a secure grasp.
Test the mouse grasp with a small vertical lift, then a short rightward translation while keeping closed.
The mouse is ahead of the fingertips, not retained. Advance the open wrist to surround its middle rather than the rear edge.
Replan after continuity rejection with smaller forward/downward increments to center the mouse and ease the elbow bend.
Close around the centered mouse, then test retention with a small backward lift and reduced pitch to ease the tight elbow configuration.
Use submillimeter lift and small backward/pitch increments after the guard interruption, keeping the mouse grasp closed.
Retention is still uncertain. Move slowly left and slightly lower to inspect contact and set up a controlled lateral transfer.
Gently guide the mouse laterally toward the pad with the closed fingertips at its left side; monitor sliding contact.
Reopen around the mouse and lower the grasp by three centimeters to engage its sides instead of the upper rear surface.
Close at the lower side-contact height and test with a small backward lift; watch whether the mouse moves with the fingers.
Transfer the mouse rightward toward the pad with closed fingers and a modest lift; check that it follows.
Mouse still not retained. Reposition to its left with a shallower wrist angle for a controlled side push onto the pad.
Bring the closed fingertips down beside the mouse at table height before the lateral push.
Make slow side contact and guide the mouse rightward and slightly toward the front of the pad.
Advance the open fingers farther around the mouse body and lower carefully to engage its sides rather than its rear tip.
Align farther forward and right around the now-rotated mouse, then close without additional descent.
Allow closure to finish with the mouse visibly between the fingers, then make a small backward lift to verify retention.
The mouse appears retained between the fingers. Carry it rightward and toward the pad center with a little clearance.
Reposition right above the mouse's left side for a lower push. Begin a separate left-arm raised approach toward the clock without crossing workspaces.
Lower right fingertips to the mouse's left side at table level; advance the open left wrist toward the clock from above.
Advance left fingers around the clock and lower gently. Move the right closed fingertips toward the mouse side to establish actual contact.
Close the left gripper around the centered clock. Continue the right side push toward the pad, watching mouse motion rather than assuming a grasp.
Lift the clock with closed left fingers to verify retention. Recenter the open right fingers around the mouse now at the pad's back edge, then close.
Carry the visibly retained clock upward and left toward the drawer. Clear the right wrist above the mouse to approach its back side for a pull toward the pad.
Raise the held clock above the drawer rim. Lower the right closed fingertips behind the mouse to guide it forward onto the pad.
After the left IK interruption, use smaller forward motion and ease wrist pitch rather than raising further. Establish low contact behind the mouse and begin a gentle pull toward the pad.
Move the retained clock farther over the drawer top before release. Gently draw the mouse toward the pad at low fingertip height.
Release the clock over the drawer top, then ease the left arm backward. Open and close the right fingers around the mouse at the current low, shallow approach.
Clock is resting on the drawer. Ease the left wrist out with very small initial increments after the guard rejection. Close on the centered mouse and test a short backward lift.
Move the left wrist clear of the placed clock toward the figurine. Advance the open right fingers farther around the mouse body; the prior closure was still behind it.
Lower the open left fingers around the figurine's upper body. Close the right fingers at the new mouse alignment, then test a short backward lift.
Center and close around the figurine's upper body. Draw the right fingertips backward toward the pad while monitoring whether the mouse follows contact.
Test figurine retention with a vertical lift. Move the open right wrist farther behind the mouse with clearance; earlier contact remained at the front end.
Carry the retained figurine toward its stand. After the right-arm guard, stop advancing and lower the open fingers around the mouse at the current position.
Align the figurine base toward the visible stand while lowering slightly. Close the right fingers behind the mouse and begin drawing it toward the pad.
The figurine slipped onto the table; reopen and approach its torso again from the front. Continue the right backward contact that is moving the mouse onto the pad.
The mouse is now on the pad; open and withdraw the right wrist. Relieve left-arm contact with the tilted figurine and recenter in front of its torso.
Refine the left torso grasp by moving rightward and back from the figurine. Withdraw the right arm away from the organized mouse toward the keyboard workspace.
Finish closing the left grasp and test a small vertical lift of the figurine. Move the right closed gripper to the keyboard's front-right approach.
Lower the open left fingers to the figurine's torso rather than its head. Align the right closed fingertips behind the keyboard's front edge.
Close the left fingers around the figurine's upper body and pause. Start a slow forward-right keyboard push from its front edge.
Recenter the open left grasp leftward and farther around the figurine. Back the right pusher away and move toward the keyboard center to reduce rotation.
Lower the open left grasp to the figurine torso, avoiding another head-only closure. Continue the keyboard's central forward-right push slowly.
Center the left fingers on the figurine's armor before closing. Retreat and recenter the right keyboard pusher to avoid adding rotation.
Test the centered torso grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping the right arm still until the figurine is secure.
Carry the figurine with its torso held closed toward the visible stand, keeping its base clear and checking retention.
Lower the retained figurine while advancing its base onto the stand marker, preserving its upright orientation.
Set the figurine base down over the stand and open the left fingers without disturbing its upright posture.
Withdraw the open left wrist from the released figurine and prepare to straighten the keyboard from its front-left side.
Bring the closed left fingertips behind the keyboard's nearer left corner, keeping the right pusher still as a reference.
Push the nearer left keyboard corner forward and slightly right to straighten it while the right pusher remains stationary.
Separate the wrists by lifting and withdrawing the right pusher outward before continuing the left-side keyboard correction.
Advance the left keyboard corner to reduce its diagonal angle while keeping the right wrist clear.
The left fingertips passed above the keyboard. Back away and lower slightly to contact its front edge instead of the keys.
Use the newly established low contact to push the near-left keyboard end forward and right, correcting its angle without moving the right wrist.
Withdraw the left fingers completely from above the keys and angle toward the keyboard's nearest end for a lower edge-contact approach.
Lower and pitch the left fingertips behind the keyboard's near end, aiming for the thin edge rather than the key surface.
Advance the low left fingertips toward the keyboard's near end to establish edge contact and rotate it toward horizontal.
Continue the low left-end keyboard push forward and right, keeping the right arm clear and watching the changing angle.
Continue the effective low left-end push toward the frame, reducing the keyboard angle while keeping the right wrist clear.
Advance the keyboard's left end mostly forward to finish straightening it and bring its center into the frame.
Make a final small left-end keyboard correction, then open and withdraw both grippers without disturbing the arranged items.
Withdraw both open wrists upward and outward from the organized items, gradually restoring the home orientation while maintaining elbow-up continuity.
